inventory.method: Every cursor advance, length computation, slice/reference formation and ownership transfer in d2i.rs was classified before editing. 'structural' means the representation cannot hold an out-of-bounds position; 'checked' means a guard at that site (usually cursor_distance/remaining_after or checked_add) refuses it.

changes: Added Cursor (pointer + remaining) with one audited unsafe constructor and checked advance, advance_to, take, limit, read_u8 and consumed_since. A cursor past the end is unrepresentable: advance/take refuse and leave the cursor unchanged.

collect and find_end now take &mut Cursor. Both call check_tlen with ctx == NULL (no TOO_LONG pre-check); their declared content is bounded by take/limit/advance before any read, closing the historical over-read/over-advance class.
check_tlen takes &mut Cursor, advances by the header only through the cursor, and derives an indefinite plen from the cursor's remaining count.
d2i_ex_primitive holds one cursor from the caller's (in_, inlen), publishes *in_ only on success, and proves the primitive/constructed/encoded extents by cursor advance instead of p.add.
check_eoc is now safe (a copy probe through read_u8); Collected::append and Collected::terminate no longer need unsafe signatures (their source/destination extents are owned or cursor-proved).
embed_d2i, mstring_d2i, template_ex_d2i and template_noexp_d2i use short-lived cursors at each check_tlen/check_eoc boundary; their remaining field accounting is unchanged checked subtraction.

cve_2026_34180_class.class: content length near or above 2 GiB narrowing to a negative or wrapped c_int
mechanism: check_tlen computes hdrlen + plen with checked_add and rejects declared > len with TOO_LONG before any content extent exists.

ex_c2i's string arm compares len with (int)len before use; OBJECT likewise; BIT STRING and OBJECT reject len > INT_MAX before reading content; INTEGER's magnitude length r is rejected when r > INT_MAX.
d2i_ex_primitive advances the cursor by the declared content before ex_c2i, so an extent the input does not hold is refused before the content pointer is consumed.
proof_tests: asn1::d2i::tests::d2i_content_length_at_i32_and_u32_boundaries_is_refused (header lengths i32::MAX, i32::MAX+1, u32::MAX and 64-bit forms; plus direct ex_c2i/ossl_c2i_ASN1_BIT_STRING/ossl_c2i_ASN1_OBJECT calls at INT_MAX+1 with a one-byte buffer)
cve_2026_34180_class.limit: A real >2 GiB content buffer is not allocated in-test; the guard is exercised at the exact boundary and the codec guards are called directly. The allocation-infeasible path is covered by code inspection, not execution.

negative_control.name: asn1::d2i::tests::d2i_canary_pre_fix_cursor_advance_would_overrun
negative_control.fires_on: the removed collect arithmetic: a declared 127-byte nested primitive with one byte remaining
negative_control.output: d2i canary: pre-fix collect would read 126 bytes past the input; post-fix cursor refused the advance and kept remaining=1
negative_control.note: It models the pre-fix distance and asserts the post-fix refusal. It is not a runtime UB detector; only Miri/ASan would observe the pre-fix read itself.

unsafe.before_after: d2i.rs: production unsafe blocks 252 -> 238; cfg(test) blocks 5 -> 14; total 257 -> 252. unsafe fn 20 -> 18 (Cursor::new added; check_eoc, Collected::append, Collected::terminate no longer unsafe).
unsafe.eliminated: 14 production unsafe blocks and 9 explicit input-pointer advance/read sites (2 raw reads + 3 advances in check_eoc, 1 advance in collect, 1 in check_tlen, 2 in d2i_ex_primitive, 2 in find_end).
unsafe.relocated: 3 raw operations now live in Cursor's safe methods (one ptr.add in advance, one read and one ptr.add in read_u8), plus the audited Cursor::new unsafe constructor. advance_to derives an offset by integer address comparison and then uses advance, so it performs no raw pointer arithmetic of its own.
unsafe.new_abstractions: none. Cursor is a safe interface whose only unsafe entry is a constructor with an explicit SAFETY contract; it is not an unsafe trait or an adoption mechanism.

discharged: Every check-eoc probe is bounded and leaves the cursor unchanged on a non-marker.
Every declared content extent is refused before it is read or advanced past, including the two ctx == NULL callers that skip TOO_LONG.
check_tlen publishes its cursor only on success and returns 0/-1 with the caller's cursor unchanged.
d2i_ex_primitive publishes *in_ only after the content codec succeeds; on every error return the Collected block is released by Drop or handed to the codec exactly once.
A failed re-decode frees the caller's previous value and nulls the slot (test).
retained: embed_d2i/template_ex_d2i/template_noexp_d2i still pass *mut *const u8 + c_long at the internal call boundary; their arithmetic is checked by cursor_distance/remaining_after (checked, not structural).
hdrlen + plen is checked_add at the site, preserving the authority's TOO_LONG error ordering.
ex_c2i still performs the authority's narrowing cast; safety rests on the guards before each use.
ASN1_get_object's omax-consumed subtraction is safe by the max-accounting invariant, audited but not rewritten (der.rs is reader scope).
introduced: A stale cached header that does not fit the current cursor now returns 0 without raising. Unreachable with a consistent ASN1_TLC; the authority would advance out of bounds.

compatibility_delta: No intended observable change for well-formed input or for the existing malformed courts. Error coordinates and ordering are unchanged. The two new refusals replace out-of-bounds behaviour (collect/find_end overlong nested elements); a refused decode still reports no progress. Existing d2i/asn1 tests plus the new boundary tests pass.
